title: Ground Beef with Egg and Onion

content.title: About
content.content: Ground beef with egg and onion is a ready‑to‑use mixture of minced beef, eggs and finely chopped onion. It is commonly used in Russian and European cuisines for making patties, meatballs, casseroles and sauces. The combination provides juiciness, aroma and an extra boost of protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally this mixture is prepared at home, but it is now available pre‑made in many supermarkets.
Eggs act as a binder, helping the meat hold together and stay tender.
Onion adds a characteristic flavor and helps retain moisture during cooking.
Beef is a rich source of iron that is more bioavailable than plant‑based iron.
The blend of beef, egg and onion is featured in classic dishes such as Kiev cutlet and meatball casseroles.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Both beef and eggs provide complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Good source of iron
items.content: Beef supplies heme iron, which is readily absorbed and supports healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The mixture contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Onion antioxidants
items.content: Onion contributes quercetin and other flavonoids with anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Balanced macronutrients
items.content: The blend offers a balance of protein, fat and a small amount of carbohydrates, making it versatile for many dietary patterns.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Fresh meat can harbor pathogens such as Salmonella or E. coli; it should be stored and cooked to at least 71 °C.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: People with egg allergy should avoid this product.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Ground beef contains saturated fats; individuals with high cholesterol should monitor portion size.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Pre‑seasoned mixes may contain added salt, which should be considered by those watching sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The mixture can be pan‑fried, sautéed, baked, or used as a filling for pies and crepes. It is commonly shaped into patties, meatballs, or added to pasta sauces. Ensure it is cooked through to eliminate any harmful bacteria.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the mixture refrigerated at 0–4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Thaw in the refrigerator before use, never at room temperature.
